subject: zoology
question_text: In which way does tobacco affect the respiration? Name the alkaloid found in tobacco.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.59, VSAQ 141). Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Effect on respiration
lines: When tobacco is smoked, the carbon monoxide
level in the blood rises and the oxygen level
Carbon monoxide binds to haemoglobin, so less
oxygen is carried to the tissues.
steps.why: The effect is on the blood's carrying capacity, not on the lungs alone, so the answer names the gas that rises and the gas that falls.
common_mistakes: Writing only that smoking is harmful to the lungs. Name carbon monoxide and oxygen.
Writing that nicotine reduces oxygen. It is carbon monoxide that does this.
steps.memory_tip: Carbon monoxide up, oxygen down: the blood carries the wrong gas.
steps.margin_note: Two short lines naming both gases. That is the whole first mark.

steps.label: The alkaloid
lines: The alkaloid found in tobacco is nicotine.
It stimulates the adrenal gland to release
adrenaline and noradrenaline, which raise the
blood pressure and the heart rate.
steps.why: Nicotine is the one name the question asks for, and the extra line shows the student knows it acts on the adrenal gland rather than on the lungs.
common_mistakes: Naming tar or carbon monoxide. Neither is an alkaloid.
Writing that nicotine is a gas. It is an alkaloid.
steps.memory_tip: One alkaloid, one name: nicotine, and it works through the adrenal gland.
steps.margin_note: The name alone earns the mark. One extra line on its action is enough.

insider_note: This is a two-part question and each part carries its own mark, so answer the respiration part in full before naming nicotine.
